summary: No new receipt this turn; I corrected a durable entry that its own new evidence had made wrong. The repair Fact still said a lost configuration can be restored by exactly three paths, but the operator-recovery receipt established a fourth — RecoverCluster on a stopped node with the configuration supplied — and also showed that live bootstrap explicitly does not work, refusing with ErrCantBootstrap whenever state exists. The Fact is revised under its existing id with a changed_premise explaining the correction rather than a silent edit: it now lists four paths (a later configuration entry from a correctly configured leader; an operator restart with the flag disabled; RecoverCluster on the stopped node; and an installed snapshot, with the boundary that no snapshot is sent to a node whose log is complete), states that only the first is in-protocol and that none works on a running node with a complete log, keeps the cluster-wide unavailability consequence and its dependency on operator action, extends the conditions to the single-voter operator scenario, adds the two new source anchors (the bootstrap refusal and RecoverCluster) and cites the operator-recovery receipt with parsed indices 1 and 2 alongside the earlier evidence. All other records are unchanged and the submission validates without execution requests.
